column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses separate finite verbs for taking a bribe and perverting judgment; BSB makes these actions participles. It has singular “a bribe,” rendered plural “bribes” in BSB.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats Samuel’s name as the subject of praying; BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew describes rejection of the LORD’s “reigning over them”; BSB expresses this as rejecting Him “as their king.”
The Hebrew says they do this to “you also”; BSB leaves the “also” implicit.
The Hebrew commands listening to “their voice”; BSB says “listen to them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “his chariot” in both occurrences; BSB uses plural “his chariots.” It names his horsemen, where BSB has “horses.”

The Hebrew pairs plowing with his plowing-land and reaping with his harvest, repeating the respective roots. It names the equipment of his chariot, where BSB turns this into the action “to equip his chariots.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names their “seed” and “vineyards”; BSB renders these as “grain and grape harvest.”
The Hebrew names their best “young men”; BSB has “best cattle.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they will “cry out” because of their king; BSB specifies that they will “beg for relief.”
The Hebrew mentions “the voice of Samuel” and says a king “shall be over us”; BSB omits the voice image and renders the demand as “We must have a king.”
The Hebrew calls the king “our king”; BSB uses “a king.”
The Hebrew says Samuel spoke the words “in the ears of the LORD”; BSB renders the bodily image as “in the hearing of the LORD.”
The Hebrew commands them to “go, each to his city”; BSB adds an explicit return in “go back.”
